questions.q: What was laid on the kitchen table for supper when David came in?
choices: Bread, cheese and a big jug of fresh warm milk
A roast chicken and a bottle of wine
Porridge, a horn spoon and a cup of small beer
Oatcakes, herring and a pot of tea
questions.evidence: a bowl of porridge, a horn spoon, and a cup of small beer

questions.q: Besides a few dishes, what else was in the bare kitchen?
choices: A fine clock and a painting of the old family laird
Shelves full of books and a writing desk
A spinning wheel and a basket of wool
Lockfast chests and a padlocked corner cupboard
questions.evidence: lockfast chests arranged along the wall and a corner cupboard with a padlock

questions.q: What troubled David most about the way the man looked at him?
choices: He kept laughing at David's dusty clothes
He stared angrily at David's letter
He would not stop staring at his face
He would not look him fairly in the face
questions.evidence: he would neither take his eyes away from me nor look me fairly in the face

questions.q: Who did the man in the nightcap turn out to be?
choices: The session clerk of Cramond parish
David's uncle, his father's brother
An old servant left to mind the house
A cousin of Mr. Campbell the minister
questions.evidence: I'm your born uncle, Davie, my man

questions.q: Uncle Ebenezer tells David to "sit down and fill your kyte." What is a "kyte"?
choices: Pipe
Pockets
Cup
Stomach
questions.evidence: sit down and fill your kyte

questions.q: When Ebenezer asks what brought him, how does David answer about hoping for help?
choices: He begs his uncle for money to go home
He says he expects to be made the laird
He admits some hope but says he is no beggar
He says he only came to see the house

questions.q: What did Uncle Ebenezer do with the porridge after David had eaten some?
choices: He saved it in a cupboard for the next morning
He took the stool and spoon and ate it himself
He gave it to a dog that lived in the kitchen
He threw it in the fire because it had gone cold
questions.evidence: as soon as he had ousted me from the stool and spoon

questions.q: How long ago had David's father died?
choices: Three weeks
Three months
Ten days
One year

questions.q: Ebenezer seemed "singularly satisfied" to learn that David's father never spoke of him or of Shaws. What does this suggest?
choices: Ebenezer thought David was lying to win his favour
Ebenezer was hurt and wanted David to leave at once
Ebenezer was proud of how quiet his brother had been
Ebenezer was glad David knew little about the family

questions.q: Why did Uncle Ebenezer refuse to give David a light for bed?
choices: He said the moon was bright enough
He said boys should sleep in the dark
He said he was afraid of fires
He said candles cost far too much

questions.q: What happened right after Uncle Ebenezer said good-night at the bedroom door?
choices: He sat outside the door all night
He locked David in from the outside
He brought David a candle after all
He came back with a warm blanket
questions.evidence: I heard him lock me in from the outside

questions.q: Where did David sleep on his first night at Shaws?
choices: On the floor beside the big bedstead, in his plaid
On a bench by the kitchen fire with his bundle
In the damp bed under a heap of old woollen blankets
In a chair by the window looking at the moon
questions.evidence: I lay down upon the floor under lee of the big bedstead

questions.q: How did Uncle Ebenezer share the one cup of beer at breakfast?
choices: He poured an exact half into another cup
He filled a second cup up from the barrel
He let David have the whole cup himself
He drank it all and gave David water
questions.evidence: he poured an accurate half from one cup to the other

questions.q: What does David decide about his uncle after the beer is shared?
choices: He is a drunkard who hides his ale
He is poor and cannot afford any food
He is a miser, but a thorough one
He is a generous and kindly host
questions.evidence: if my uncle was certainly a miser

questions.q: What did Uncle Ebenezer ask David not to do while he thought about David's future?
choices: Walk in the garden or near the stairs
Go down to the village or speak to Jennet
Open the chests or the padlocked cupboard
Send any letters or messages to anybody
questions.evidence: Nae letters; nae messages; no kind of word to onybody

questions.q: How did Uncle Ebenezer react when David gave him Jennet Clouston's message?
choices: He said he would pay her money to stop cursing his house
He called her a witch and wanted to see the session clerk
He laughed and said she was a harmless old neighbour
He turned pale and hid himself in the upstairs rooms
questions.evidence: A witch--a proclaimed witch! I'll aff and see the session clerk

questions.q: Why did Uncle Ebenezer decide not to go out after all?
choices: He saw Jennet Clouston coming toward the house
He found that his old blue coat was too worn to wear
He suddenly remembered that the session clerk was away
David said locking him out would end their friendship

questions.q: Why does David think Uncle Ebenezer works so hard to keep him at Shaws?
choices: He cannot tell; his uncle seems to dislike him yet wants him to stay
He knows his uncle means him to marry a rich neighbour's daughter now
He believes his uncle needs a servant to help with the house
He thinks his uncle is lonely and wants a son to share his meals
questions.evidence: I can make nothing out of this

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: David meeting his strange, miserly uncle and agreeing to stay awhile
David returning to Essendean after his uncle sends him away
David and his uncle visiting the village to confront Jennet
David exploring the house and finding a secret room full of gold
